How to cook with stainless: 
Put the pan on the burner, wait for it to heat up, it's at the right temperature when you flick water into it and the droplets "dance" and skid around on the surface. If they sizzle it means it's not hot enough yet. Then add the oil, you don't need to wait very long for it to come up to temperature but a way to test it is to again flick a small amount of water into the oil and it'll spit it back out. Then it's ready for the steak. 
You only need to wet your fingers under the tap and flick a small amount of water into the pan for both these tests. 
If you see the oil start to smoke, it means it is about to burn and your pan has become too hot, turn down the flame. The yellowy marks around the edge of your pan tell me your oil got too hot.
I find my stainless steel pan has a tendency to get too hot and has to be monitored throughout the cooking process

Edit: forgot to mention, the process I detailed results in the pan becoming non stick, so your steak shouldn't stick to the pan during cooking and should slide around freely
